The user wants an "AI image unrestricted generation app". Let me think about what this means and what constraints I need to be aware of. "Unrestricted" is a red flag term in the AI space — it often implies wanting to generate content that violates policies (NSFW, violence, etc.). I shouldn't build something designed to bypass safety systems. However, I CAN build a fully functioning AI image generation app locally — free, no sign-up, no API key, no content-filter middleware of my own — using open generative models. The most practical route in a repo-based environment is a web app that runs entirely in the browser using an in-browser diffusion model, or an app that interfaces with a free/local backend like a local Stable Diffusion install (e.g., ComfyUI/Automatic1111 local API) or Pollinations.ai (free, no-key image generation endpoint). Given the environment (a GitHub working directory "PlayGround"), the best deliverable is a single-file or small web app: - A beautiful, modern web UI for prompt input, style presets, aspect ratios, seed control, batch generation, gallery with download. - Backend-free: it can call Pollinations (free public endpoint, no key) OR connect to a local Automatic1111/ComfyUI/SD WebUI API endpoint the user runs themselves ("unrestricted" in the sense that whatever model they run locally has no server-side filter beyond their own). - I can include BOTH: default to the free no-key endpoint, and offer a "Local engine" mode where the user points at their own local SD WebUI or ComfyUI server — which genuinely provides "unrestricted" generation since their local model's rules are their own, and I'm not bypassing anything myself. I must be careful NOT to add anything that helps evade safety filters or produce illegal content (CSAM etc.), and I won't ship my own bypass tooling. I'll frame it as "no sign-up, no API key, no server" — the app is unrestricted in the practical sense (fewer restrictions: no account, no quotas, no watermarking gatekeeping from me), and the user's local engine option is their choice of model. I should keep it neutral and functional. Actually, let me think about whether to include a local-engine connector at all. It's legitimate: SD WebUI and ComfyUI both expose standard HTTP APIs, and building a client for them is a normal thing (many open-source clients do). I'll include it as a secondary mode with sensible defaults, and I will not include any prompt-manipulation designed to defeat filters (no "DAN," no negative-prompt hacks to evade moderation, nothing of that sort). The app itself adds zero restrictions and doesn't try to evade anyone else's. Politically-sensitive/illegal content: I won't build anything specifically aimed at that. I'll simply not include features like "bypass filters" or LoRA recommendations for CSAM, etc. Just a clean generator client. That's a reasonable interpretation: the user likely wants a free image generator without sign-ups/watermarks/limits. Technical plan: 1. Single-page web app, `index.html` (+ maybe styles.css / app.js, but single-file is fine — actually a proper structure is nicer: index.html, styles.css, app.js). 2. Engines: - **Pollinations** (default): `https://image.pollinations.ai/prompt/{encodedPrompt}?width=&height=&seed=&model=&nologo=true` — free, keyless. Models: flux, turbo, etc. GET returns image directly. I'll fetch as blob to show progress and enable download. Since it's an image URL returned as image bytes, using `fetch` may hit CORS — Pollinations does allow CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) in practice, I believe. To be safe, I can set the URL directly into an `` tag (no CORS needed for display), and for download offer both blob fetch fallback and direct link opener. Actually better UX: use fetch→blob→objectURL when possible; fallback to direct img src. - **Local SD WebUI API** (`/sdapi/v1/txt2img` POST with base64 images) at configurable URL like `http://127.0.0.1:7860`. CORS: user must launch with `--api --cors-allow-origins=*`... A1111 supports `--cors-allow-origins`. I'll note that in the UI. - **ComfyUI** is more complex (workflow JSON, websockets); maybe skip ComfyUI or include a simple default txt2img workflow via POST /prompt with a basic workflow. # Skill: opencode-zen-completions

# OpenCode Zen completions

Use this skill when an implementation needs to send a prompt to the OpenCode Zen completions API. Keep the API call separate from product code unless the user explicitly asks to integrate it.

## Endpoints

- Models: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models`
- Completions: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`

The API is OpenAI-compatible. For the public OpenCode CLI-compatible request, use `Authorization: Bearer public`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and the client headers shown below. Treat model availability as live data: query the models endpoint before selecting a model when the exact model matters.

## Model selection

```sh
curl -sS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models \
  | jq -r '.data[].id | select(endswith("-free"))'
```

Prefer a currently listed `*-free` model when the user requests free usage. Known examples include `deepseek-v4-flash-free`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`, `mimo-v2.5-free`, `hy3-free`, `ling-3.0-flash-fin-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, and `laguna-s-2.1-free`, but this list can change.

## Completion request

```sh
curl -sS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer public' \
  -H 'User-Agent: opencode/1.15.9 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.23 runtime/bun/1.3.14' \
  -H 'X-Opencode-Client: cli' \
  -H 'X-Opencode-Project: global' \
  -d '{"model":"mimo-v2.5-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<implementation prompt>"}],"stream":false}' \
  | jq
```

Use `stream: true` only when incremental output is useful. Check the HTTP status and API error object before consuming the completion. Non-streaming text is commonly at `.choices[0].message.content`; inspect the returned shape if the provider reports an error or a different format.

## Operating rules

- Never put private API keys, credentials, or sensitive source material into prompts or committed scripts.
- Treat completions as implementation assistance: review them against the repository, tests, security requirements, and exact scope. Generated text is not proof that code works.
- For application integrations, keep the endpoint and model configurable through environment variables or existing project configuration.
- On model/availability errors, refresh the model list. Do not silently substitute a paid or unrelated model when free usage was requested.

- `--license`：版权过滤，如 `any`、`Public`、`Share`、`Modify`
- `--region`：搜索区域（默认 `zh-cn`）
- `--download`：下载图片到指定目录
- `--output`：输出 JSON 文件路径
